facts.statement: Wiehenvenator was a megalosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in northwestern Germany during the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage.
facts.quote: Wiehenvenator is a genus of megalosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic (Callovian) of north western Germany.

facts.statement: The remains of Wiehenvenator were discovered in 1998 by geologist Friedrich Albat at the Pott quarry in the Wiehen Hills near Minden, Westphalia.
facts.quote: In 1998, geologist Friedrich Albat, prospecting for the Landschaftsverband Westfalen-Lippe Museum of Natural History, discovered the remains of a large theropod at the abandoned Pott quarry in the Wiehen Hills near Minden, Westphalia.

facts.statement: The discovery was initially known informally as the 'Minden Monster' due to extensive media attention.
facts.quote: The find received extensive press attention and was informally known as Das Monster von Minden (the Minden Monster).

facts.statement: The species was formally named Wiehenvenator albati in 2016 by Rauhut, Hübner, and Lanser.
facts.quote: In 2016, the fossils were named and described as the type species Wiehenvenator albati by Oliver W. M. Rauhut, Tom R. Hübner and Klaus-Peter Lanser.

facts.statement: The species name albati honors the discoverer, Friedrich Albat.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Friedrich Albat, the discoverer.

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of various bones from the Ornatenton Formation dating to the middle Callovian.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Wiehenvenator consists of an assortment of bones found in the Ornatenton Formation dating from the middle Callovian.

facts.statement: The fossil includes skull parts, jaw fragments, six teeth, tail vertebrae, ribs, a finger bone, leg bones, and ankle bones.
facts.quote: They include parts of the skull (right premaxilla, right maxilla, right lacrimal bone, right postorbital and possible front branch of the right quadratojugal), the anterior parts of a right lower jaw (dentary), six teeth, three tail vertebrae, a pair of fused median segments of rear gastralia, one complete rib and four rib fragments, a finger phalanx, both fibulae, a right astragalus and a right calcaneum.

facts.statement: Bone analysis suggests the individual was at least nine years old, possibly over ten, when it died.
facts.quote: Histological analysis of its fibulae suggests that the holotype of Wiehenvenator albati was at least in its ninth year of life, however, the age at death might have been well over ten years.

facts.statement: Growth analysis indicates the specimen was a large subadult with slowing skeletal growth.
facts.quote: The remains indicated that the animal was actively growing, but narrow growth zones indicated that the skeletal growth rate was slowing down. From this it can be determined that the growth state of Wiehenvenator was that of a large subadult individual.

facts.statement: Its maxilla is 82% the length of Torvosaurus gurneyi's maxilla, which is estimated at 10 meters.
facts.quote: The length of Wiehenvenator can be estimated by extrapolating from its maxilla, which has 82 percent of the length of the maxilla of Torvosaurus gurneyi, itself estimated at 10 m.

facts.statement: Its tail vertebrae and fibulae match those of Torvosaurus tanneri (estimated at 9m), making it one of the largest known European theropods.
facts.quote: Another estimate can be gleaned from the fact that its tail vertebrae and fibulae are roughly equal in length to those of Torvosaurus tanneri, which had been estimated at 9 m, thus making Wiehenvenator one of the largest known European theropods.

facts.statement: Mickey Mortimer estimated the skull length at nearly 1 meter and the total length at 7 to 8 meters with a weight of 0.75 to 1.2 tons.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Mickey Mortimer, el maxilar, el hueso que sostiene a la mayoría de los dientes superiores en el cráneo, mide unos 51,7 centímetros de largo, lo que sugiere una longitud craneal de cerca de 1 metro, junto con una fíbula de 75 centímetros, lo que indica que pertenecían a un individuo en el rango de 7 a 8 metros de longitud y 0,75 a 1,2 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Wiehenvenator is classified within the Megalosauridae family as a sister taxon to Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2016, Wiehenvenator was placed in the Megalosauridae as a sister taxon to Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: Wiehenvenator belongs to the superfamily Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Megalosauroidea

facts.statement: A report of a rib 50% larger than Allosaurus sparked speculation that the animal could reach 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: Reports in the German edition of the National Geographic of a rib 50% larger than that of Allosaurus stirred speculations that it reached 15 m in length.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Wiehenvenator at 12 meters in 2012.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz estimated it at 12 m in 2012.

facts.statement: Other researchers concluded smaller dimensions, with Mickey Mortimer estimating a length of 7 to 8 meters and a weight of 0.75 to 1.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: Other researchers concluded to smaller dimensions: Mickey Mortimer in 2003 estimated the animal to be 7 to 8 m in length and 0.75 to 1.2 MT in weight.

facts.statement: Excavation teams returned to the site to search for additional material after the initial discovery.
facts.quote: After discovering the initial remains of Wiehenvenator, members of the excavation team returned to the site and continued to search the surroundings for further material.

facts.statement: Searching 35 meters around the formation yielded remains of the marine reptile Liopleurodon.
facts.quote: After searching 35m both east and west of the Ornatenton Formation, some weathered vertebral centra and teeth of Liopleurodon were found.

facts.statement: A second theropod was found 28.5 meters northwest of the original site in October 1999.
facts.quote: One year later, in mid-October 1999, the remains consisting of a maxillary fragment, bone fragments, and a tooth, of a second theropod were found 28.5 m north-west of the first locality.

facts.statement: The crocodylomorph Metriorhynchus was discovered in an overgrown quarry in October 2014.
facts.quote: On October 3, 2014, in an overgrown quarry to the west, the skull and lower jaws of the crocodylomorph Metriorhynchus were discovered by an honorary member of the LWL Museum für Naturkunde.

facts.statement: Friedrich Albat discovered the remains of a large theropod in 1998 at the abandoned Pott quarry in the Wiehen hills near Minden, Westphalia, Germany.
facts.quote: En 1998, el geólogo Friedrich Albat, que realizaba prospecciones para el Museo de Historia Natural Landschaftsverband Westfalen-Lippe, descubrió los restos de un gran terópodo en la cantera abandonada de Pott en las colinas Wiehen, cerca de Minden, Westfalia, Alemania.

facts.statement: The fragmentary theropod skeleton was excavated between October 1998 and October 2001 alongside abundant marine invertebrates and fossilized wood.
facts.quote: El esqueleto fragmentario de terópodo, encontrado junto a abundantes invertebrados marinos y madera fosilizada, fue excavado entre octubre de 1998 y octubre de 2001.

facts.statement: The discovery received significant press attention and was informally known as Das Monster von Minden (The Monster of Minden).
facts.quote: El hallazgo recibió una gran atención de la prensa y se conoció informalmente como Das Monster von Minden (el Monstruo de Minden).

facts.statement: Initial reports in the German edition of National Geographic noted a rib 50% larger than that of Allosaurus, leading to speculation that the animal could reach over 15 meters in length.
facts.quote: Hubo reportes iniciales en la edición alemana de National Geographic de una costilla 50% más grande que la de Allosaurus, lo que llevó a especular con que podría llegar a medir más de 15 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of fibulae indicates the known specimen of Wiehenvenator was a large subadult approximately ten years old when it died.
facts.quote: El análisis histológico de las fíbulas indica que el espécimen conocido de Wiehenvenator es un individuo subadulto grande, de cerca de diez años de edad al momento de morir.

facts.statement: The fossil remains include parts of the skull, premaxilla, maxilla, a possible lacrimal bone, postorbital bones, the anterior part of a dentary, teeth, fused gastralia, two tail vertebrae, a complete rib, four rib fragments, an ilium, fibulae, and other elements.
facts.quote: El esqueleto fragmentario de terópodo, encontrado junto a abundantes invertebrados marinos y madera fosilizada, fue excavado entre octubre de 1998 y octubre de 2001.

facts.statement: Oliver W. M. Rauhut, Tom R. Hübner, and Klaus-Peter Lanser named and described the type species Wiehenvenator albati in 2016.
facts.quote: En 2016, los fósiles fueron nombrados y descritos como la especie tipo Wiehenvenator albati por Oliver W. M. Rauhut, Tom R. Hübner y Klaus-Peter Lanser.

facts.statement: The generic name combines a reference to Wiehengebirge, the German name for the Wiehen hills, with the Latin word venator, meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico combina una referencia a Wiehengebirge , el nombre alemán de las colinas Wiehen, con un latín venator, por "cazador".

facts.statement: The specific name honors Friedrich Albat, the discoverer of the fossils.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra a Friedrich Albat, el descubridor.

facts.statement: Wiehenvenator was classified in 2016 in the family Megalosauridae, specifically in the subfamily Megalosaurinae, as the sister taxon to Torvosaurus, its closest relative.
facts.quote: Wiehenvenator fue clasificado en 2016 en la familia Megalosauridae, más concretamente en la subfamilia Megalosaurinae, colocado como taxón hermano de Torvosaurus, su pariente más cercano.

facts.statement: Wiehenvenator lived during the Callovian stage, approximately 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: A megalosaurid pedal phalanx, WMNM P27698 and WMNM P27693, found in two parts during October 1999 and April 2000, may have belonged to the holotype of W. albati.
facts.quote: Una falange pedal megalosauroide, WMNM P27698, WMNM P27693) de la Formación Ornatenton descubierta en dos partes durante octubre de 1999 y abril de 2000 puede haber pertenecido al holotipo de W. albati.

facts.statement: In mid-October 1999, remains consisting of a maxilla fragment, bone fragments, and a tooth of a second theropod were found 28.5 meters northwest of the first locality.
facts.quote: Un año después, a mediados de octubre de 1999, se encontraron los restos consistentes en un fragmento maxilar, fragmentos óseos y un diente, de un segundo terópodo a 28,5 metros al noroeste de la primera localidad.
